title: AMD 2022 Form 10-K — MD&A Expenses: R&D, MG&A, amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, licensing gain
key_points: R&D expense was $5.0B in FY2022, up $2.2B or 76%, versus $2.8B in FY2021.
The R&D increase is attributed primarily to strategic investments across all segments, including headcount increase through acquisitions and organic growth.
MG&A expense was $2.3B in FY2022, up $888M or 61%, versus $1.4B in FY2021.
The MG&A increase is attributed primarily to headcount increase through acquisitions and organic growth, go-to-market activities, and acquisition-related costs.
In FY2022, cost of sales included $1.4B and operating expense included $2.1B of amortization expense from intangible assets acquired via the Xilinx and Pensando acquisitions.
FY2022 licensing gain of $102M came from milestone achievement and royalty income on IP licensed to the THATIC JV; FY2021 licensing gain from royalty income was $12M.
Interest expense was $88M in FY2022 versus $34M in FY2021, attributed to the assumed Xilinx notes and 2022 notes.

key_points: FY2022 net revenue was $23.6B, up 44% versus FY2021 net revenue of $16.4B.

title: AMD 2022 Form 10-K — Item 7 MD&A, Results of Operations: Client segment (p48)
key_points: Client net revenue was $6.2 billion in FY2022, a 10% decrease from $6.9 billion in FY2021.
The Client revenue decline was primarily driven by a 24% decrease in unit shipments, partially offset by a 19% increase in average selling price.
The unit shipment decrease was attributed to challenging PC market conditions and significant inventory correction across the PC supply chain experienced during the second half of 2022.
The increase in average selling price was primarily driven by a richer mix of Ryzen mobile processor sales.
Client operating income was $1.2 billion in FY2022 versus $2.1 billion in FY2021; the decrease was primarily driven by lower revenue and higher operating expenses.
Data Center net revenue was $6 billion in FY2022, up 64% from $3.7 billion in FY2021, primarily driven by higher sales of EPYC server processors.
Data Center operating income was $1.8 billion in FY2022 versus $991 million in FY2021, driven by higher revenue partially offset by higher operating expenses.

Segment operating income FY2022 vs FY2021: Data Center $1,848M vs $991M; Client $1,190M vs $2,088M; Gaming $953M vs $934M; Embedded $2,252M vs $44M; All Other $(4,979)M vs $(409)M; Total $1,264M vs $3,648M.
Segment net revenue FY2022 vs FY2021: Data Center $6,043M vs $3,694M; Client $6,201M vs $6,887M; Gaming $6,805M vs $5,607M; Embedded $4,552M vs $246M; Total $23,601M vs $16,434M.
AMD changed its reporting segments in Q2 fiscal 2022 to four reportable segments: Data Center, Client, Gaming, and Embedded.
